scope: Open review of methacholine challenge as the common direct bronchoprovocation test, focused on how drugs inhibit the response and how long that effect lasts.

keyRecommendations.text: Methacholine challenge is the most common direct bronchoprovocation test. Washout of drugs that affect the response is part of standardisation.
Long-acting anti-muscarinic agents can bronchoprotect for up to 7 days, longer than their bronchodilation.
A single dose of ICS or a leukotriene-receptor antagonist does not affect the test; regular ICS use does.

clinicalBottomLine: Before a methacholine test, withhold drugs that bronchoprotect. Long-acting antimuscarinics may affect the test for up to 7 days. A single controller dose does not, but regular ICS use does.
notableCaveats: The 2017 ERS methacholine technical standard is not in PMC. This review covers pharmacology and washout, not the full dosing protocol.
